Alice Moreau · 20h
Six months ago we moved the whole reporting stack from a nightly batch to a stream, and I promised the team a retrospective once the dust had settled.

The dust has settled. Here is what I would do again, and what I would not.

I would again start with the boring half: naming the events before writing a line of code, and making the names survive a review by somebody who does not work on the team. Half of the pain of the old system came from three different words for the same thing, and no amount of engineering fixes a vocabulary problem.

I would not again run the two systems side by side for a whole quarter. We told ourselves it was insurance; what it actually bought was two systems to maintain and a team that could never quite say which of them was the truth.
Bob Nowak · 1d
Hiring for a team of four taught me more about writing job adverts than any course ever did. The first advert we published described the person we wished existed, and it brought us forty applications from people who had learned to describe themselves the same way. The second described the work: the systems that would be theirs on the first morning, the meetings they would be expected to run by the second month, and the parts of the job nobody enjoys. It brought us eleven applications, and we hired two of them, and both are still here three years later.

Dave Okafor · 3d
The warehouse ran on a spreadsheet for eleven years and the only reason it worked is that one person opened it every morning at six and closed it every evening at seven, and in between she answered the phone. When she retired we replaced her with a system that cost more than her salary and still calls her twice a month to ask what the column called "hold 2" is for.
Erin Vasquez · 4d
Every team I have joined had one document that everybody quoted and nobody had read, and finding it in the first week is the cheapest way to understand what the team believes about itself and about its work. Mine is usually a page written by somebody who left long ago, and the useful part is never the plan it contains but the problem it was written to settle.
